annotation.cut_point:
We are asked to find the **smallest 10-digit number** such that the **sum of its digits is greater than that of any smaller number**.

---

### Step 1: Understand the Problem

We are looking for the **smallest 10-digit number** $ N $ such that:

$$
\text{sum of digits of } N > \text{sum of digits of any number less than } N
$$

So, $ N $ must be the **smallest 10-digit number** with the **maximum possible digit sum** among all 10-digit numbers.

verified_state: The target number N has exactly 10 digits.
The condition is: for every number M < N, the digit sum of N is greater than the digit sum of M.
reflection.error_step: So, $ N $ must be the **smallest 10-digit number** with the **maximum possible digit sum** among all 10-digit numbers.
reflection.error_reason: This confuses a new record digit sum with the maximum possible digit sum. The condition only requires N's digit sum to exceed all smaller numbers, so N can be the first number to exceed the previous maximum (81), not necessarily the number with the absolute maximum digit sum (90).
reflection.new_direction: Find the smallest 10-digit number whose digit sum exceeds the maximum digit sum of every smaller number, starting with the previous maximum of 81 for numbers below 10 digits.
